variants.headline: A company goes under
variants.sub: The colony has seen the failure of {company}.
variants.body:
The company {company} has gone under. The failure is a business event, not a detailed account of its consequences for particular people. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known outcome from unreported claims about creditors, employment or the circumstances that brought the company to this position.

Our principles ask how an economy serves the colony, including when an enterprise fails. Our principles require political attention that keeps the purpose of public responsibility firmly in view here.

variants.headline: Business failure enters the colony's record
variants.body:
The colony has seen the failure of {company}. An enterprise is more than a name in a commercial register, but its failure does not by itself identify every consequence. An assessment of {target} should address stewardship without supplying a balance sheet or a story about the firm's trade.

Our principles ask how an economy serves the colony, including when an enterprise fails. Our principles require political attention that keeps the purpose of public responsibility firmly in view here.

variants.headline: An enterprise reaches failure
variants.body:
The business {company} has gone under. That outcome invites questions of responsibility without answering them all. For {target}, the relevant scrutiny should remain separate from an invented cause, a presumed creditor loss or an announcement about workers that the report does not establish.

Our principles ask how an economy serves the colony, including when an enterprise fails. Our principles require political attention that keeps the purpose of public responsibility firmly in view here.
